messages.author: 871ad502d7c6e556
messages.subject: Shiny -> Excel
parts:
Hi All,
I have a tool which I've developed which reads an uploaded excel file of a schools energy usage using XLConnect and outputs graphs, data tables, etc...  It recently came up at a company meeting that if we could make it so that schools were able to enter data not only into the Excel file but could also use Shiny to write to Excel, it would be perfect.  I know writing to local files is generally difficult since it's a security issue, but I was wondering if anyone had encountered a similar situation and had any suggestions for how to implement something like this?  
Thanks,
Jesse

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny -> Excel
parts:
It's not particularly a security issue as long as you only write to a temp file. Shiny has a built-in feature for generating files for download that should work in most environments:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/download.html

So the main thing you'll need to figure out is to how to write the actual Excel file. Or just use write.csv if it's only tabular data you want to return.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny -> Excel
parts:
Thanks for your reply Joe,
The problem is that the excel file I want to write to is a rather large (10 or so sheets) file used for analyzing energy usage, possible efficiency issues and solutions, emissions, etc in Oregon public schools.  We have several tools which work with and on the file for a variety of reasons, meaning that the directory of the file shouldn't change.  I'm able to write to temp files using XLConnect, however I was looking at editing the file wherever it is stored.  The current solution I'll be working on as soon as I get done with a side project is making it write and save to a cloud from which each school has access to their own file and can edit it.   I'm assuming this is possible, but haven't got a chance to try it yet.
-Jesse
